items.title: Economists warn fuel price cut likely to come with 'sting in the tail'
items.description: Australians will pay about 26.3 cents less on every litre of fuel they buy for three months, but some economists warn it could ultimately leave Australians worse off.

items.title: Live: Trump wants to 'take the oil' in Iran, as PM urges service stations to 'do the right thing'
items.description: US President Donald Trump says he wanted to "take the oil" in Iran. Follow our live coverage.

items.title: Albanese wants Trump to recognise damage Iran war has caused
items.description: Anthony Albanese wants "more certainty" from the United States on its war objectives in Iran and says the administration must be clear if it is still pursuing regime change.

items.title: From 'AI factory' to laid off: Former PwC staffer issues warning
items.description: Tasked with training AI systems to perform jobs traditionally done by humans, former PwC employee Donald King says he faced a moral dilemma.

items.title: No clear evidence ANU's course and job cuts were needed, draft report finds
items.description: ANU's council approved a massive $250 million cost-cutting program without clear evidence it was needed or achievable, according to an assessment in a draft audit office report.

items.title: Live: Victorian premier says 'an evil man is dead' after Dezi Freeman killed in police stand off
items.description: The 56-year-old had been a fugitive since a shooting at his property that killed two police officers.

items.title: Secret tunnels used in plot to smuggle one tonne of cocaine into Australia, police say
items.description: Australian police have charged six crew members of the high-profile MV Raider vessel with drug smuggling, saying they attempted to bring 1 tonne of cocaine into Australia after being intercepted by French Polynesian authorities earlier this year.

items.title: Banned Xerri reveals Essendon abuse leading to blood-wiping incident
items.description: Kangaroos ruckman Tristan Xerri gives evidence at the AFL tribunal as he accepts a suspension for rubbing blood from his nose on the face of Essendon captain Andrew McGrath.

items.title: Apocalyptic scenes from Australia ahead of cyclone make worldwide news
items.description: Cyclone Narelle turned the sky over parts of Western Australia's north into an ominous red, sparking headlines across the globe.

items.title: Israel posts fake photo of journalist it killed in strike
items.description: The IDF has admitted the image of a killed journalist in military uniform it posted on its official X account was faked.

items.title: 'Breaking point': Ex-greyhound racing insider speaks out as inquiry begins
items.description: A former greyhound racing insider tells how he reached "breaking point" with the industry, as a parliamentary inquiry into the sport in WA begins.

items.title: Which states have introduced free public transport amid fuel crisis
items.description: As fuel prices continue to rise some states have moved to make public transport free, while others say that fares are already low enough. Find out where.

items.title: Coroner finds paramedic who made 'man flu' comments failed to meet standards
items.description: A coroner has recommended the South Australian Ambulance Service consider implementing an inclusive language program after an inquest heard an Indian national was told he was overreacting with the "man flu" in the days before he died of chronic pneumonia.

items.title: 'Pretty disappointing': Star Manly recruit baffled by Seibold sacking
items.description: Jamal Fogarty finds it hard to believe that the man who convinced him to join the Sea Eagles has been shown the door after just three games working together this season.

items.title: Five easy seafood dinners for busy weeknights
items.description: Looking for tasty, hassle-free seafood meals to add to your menu?  Here are some of our favourites, from prawn pasta and tuna mornay to baked salmon and tuna cakes.

items.title: Photos explore psychological drama of Australian rural life
items.description: Western Australian documentary photographer Brad Rimmer's beautiful, melancholy images of Wheatbelt life sprawl through Fremantle gallery.

items.title: How to discuss additional work-from-home days with your employer
items.description: With rising fuel prices adding additional financial stress to household living costs, what are your rights when it comes to working from home — and what are the best ways to approach your employer about flexible work arrangements?

items.title: Parents, students demand action against 'shocking' high school bullying
items.description: Rally organisers claim there are no consequences for perpetrators and say the issue goes beyond one school or town.

items.title: Trio charged over allegedly stealing wallets from elderly shoppers
items.description: Police allege three Romanian nationals would monitor victims, some aged between 70 and 94, as they used ATM machines or paid for groceries.

items.title: Coroner calls for stricter gun laws after father-son murder-suicide
items.description: An inquest into a father-son murder-suicide has led the NSW Coroner to recommend that doctors be legally required to alert police if they have concerns about patients who own guns.

items.title: Townsville mother found not guilty of manslaughter over drowning of two sons
items.description: Townsville mother Leeanne Eatts has been found not guilty of the manslaughter of her two sons who drowned in the Ross River in February 2019.

items.title: Former NSW police officer pleads guilty to weapons charges
items.description: Jonathan James Martin has pleaded guilty to three weapons charges, and not guilty to 17 other weapons-related charges.

items.title: Former accountant jailed after defrauding Toowoomba theatre of $850k
items.description: A man has pleaded guilty in Toowoomba District Court today to two counts of fraud as an employee, with one of those fraud charges involving more than $100,000.

items.title: Storm forward hospitalised after suspected stroke in 'medical episode'
items.description: The Melbourne Storm say Tui Kamikamica is receiving the best possible care after being rushed to a hospital following a "medical episode" this morning.

items.title: Decisions made more than a decade ago are coming home to roost
items.description: The early 2010s were the years of peak globalisation, when it seemed all trade barriers were on a one-way trip to elimination. That was before Donald Trump arrived and ruptured the global order.
